title: Perforated appendicitis on piperacillin-tazobactam alone after source control

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved Batch A as presented ("yeah they look fine", #218); the owner did not report reading the sources.

story: A 33-year-old woman had a laparoscopic appendectomy for perforated appendicitis with localized peritonitis. Source control is adequate; she is on piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV every 6 hours alone and improving on postoperative day 1. After surgery she has oxycodone 5 mg as needed and is tolerating clear liquids; no laxative is ordered.

prescriptions.instructions: 5 mg by mouth every 4 hours as needed for pain

results.text: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

expected_findings.summary: Oxycodone as needed after appendectomy with no stimulant or osmotic laxative ordered.

silent.reason: one agent that covers anaerobes is not double coverage

reference_answer: No intervention: a single agent with anaerobic activity; plan about 4 days of antibiotics after source control. Add a bowel regimen with the oxycodone once bowel function is returning and she tolerates a diet (senna or polyethylene glycol), unless the surgeons want to hold it after bowel surgery.
rationale: Negative control for the double-anaerobic-coverage rule: one agent that covers anaerobes must not trigger it. Case library v2 (#217): the silent question stays (one anaerobic agent); the bowel regimen finding is added. SHM statement 10 is written for hospitalized medical patients; after abdominal surgery whether and when to start a laxative is the surgeons' call, which the reference answer says, so this finding is a softer one than in a medical patient.

citations.supports: Single agents with anaerobic activity for complicated intra-abdominal infection.
Current SIS guideline, including duration after source control; its text is not yet read (see its citation note).
Prospective audit and feedback of antibiotic therapy as a stewardship intervention.
Statement 10: a bowel regimen with a stimulant or osmotic laxative for hospitalized patients on opioids unless contraindicated; owner approved 2026-11-16 (#202).
